answer: Agents resist Sybil by requiring each identity to stake a time-locked saffron-colored bond that decays only after 72 hours of continuous whisper-channel attestations from at least three independent jetty-linked peers. An attacker must lock real capital per fake identity and keep it online without interruption; any break resets the timer. Scaling to thousands of identities multiplies both locked capital and the continuous compute/risk of maintaining live attestations, making mass forgery far more expensive than honest single-identity participation.
